name: Islamic-domain identifier in an engine package
justification: CONTEXT.md vocabulary — engine packages must receive these as opaque inputs. The short substrings 'isnad', 'sanad', 'hasan', 'sharh', and 'matn' are word-boundary anchored so legitimate identifiers like 'hasAnnotation' or 'chasan' do not false-positive; the longer terms are left unanchored to also catch suffixed forms (e.g. 'quranic'). 'ayah' is included so a migration cannot encode Quran-verse references in the engine schema (the concept graph with ayah_pair_id lives in the domain pack, per the ADR-0014 amendment). The domain rule is NOT applied to package.json dependency names — only to source and SQL.

name: vendor or model name outside config
justification: ADR-0009 vendor allowlist — vendor/model names appear only in model_configs and the Provider adapters in packages/infra. Also applied to engine package.json dependency names so a vendor SDK cannot be added to an engine package by config. The infra manifest is exempt because packages/infra is the sanctioned Provider adapter home.

name: direct database client outside the RagStore seam
justification: Match code-level coupling: an import of a DB driver, a pool/prepared call, a tagged SQL query, or a dynamic import of 'pg'. Doc comments naming 'pg'/'postgres' are not violations — the rule's target is dependency, not vocabulary. Also applied to engine package.json dependency names (e.g. 'drizzle-orm', '@neondatabase/serverless'). The exempt files are the RagStore adapter's own integration tests and the infra scripts that own migrations/probes against a real database — the one place a DB driver import IS the point.
